title: Experimenting with an AI-friendly game engine in TypeScript
author: Over_Value1408
selftext:
I’ve been tinkering with something a little unusual: building a game engine in TypeScript, but with a twist — it’s designed to be more AI-friendly.

The idea came after trying to get AI to work with existing engines like Phaser. They’re great, but I kept running into little friction points where the AI would stumble. Instead of forcing the AI to adapt, I wondered: what if the engine itself could adapt to the AI?

For example, when an AI “hallucinates” and calls a variable or function that doesn’t exist, the engine could just handle it gracefully — maybe even implement it on the fly so the same mistake doesn’t repeat. Basically, it’s about reducing those “oops, doesn’t compile” moments and smoothing the workflow.

It’s still very much a work in progress, but it’s far enough along that I’m excited to share more soon. For now, I just wanted to put this idea out there in case it resonates with anyone who’s also been experimenting with AI-driven dev workflows.
